media_placeholder_hints._note: Use exactly one hint per section; never use boolean true. The Designer makes the final call — these are editorial signals, not mandates.
media_placeholder_hints.map: data has a geographic dimension (locations, regions, routes, coordinates).
media_placeholder_hints.video: section describes an event, action, transformation, or process.
media_placeholder_hints.image: emotional beat, atmosphere, or scene that data alone cannot convey.
media_placeholder_hints.audio: every story carries a real sourced background track for mood while reading (a now-playing card, never AI-composed) — BGM is mandatory on every blog, so this hint applies by default; additionally the topic may involve music, sound, an opt-in atmospheric SFX cue for an un-findable sound, or a genuinely decodable sonic pattern.
media_placeholder_hints.interactive: reader should explore, discover, or participate (quiz, demo, slider, scrollytelling).
media_placeholder_hints.instance: a concrete embeddable example from detective.json (inst_xx) should appear here.

instance_placeholder: [INSTANCE: inst_xx] — when a concrete real-world example (a song to listen to, a photo to see, a sound to hear) should appear. Reference an inst_xx ID from detective.json's instances array. Only use when the instance makes the reader experience the data point rather than just read about it.

multimodal_awareness.geographic_data: cities, countries, coordinates, routes → flag [MEDIA: map].
multimodal_awareness.events_processes: events, incidents, anecdotes, processes → flag [MEDIA: video].
multimodal_awareness.sound: music, sound, rhythm, acoustic data → flag [MEDIA: audio].
multimodal_awareness.surprising: surprising findings the reader should guess first → flag [MEDIA: interactive].
multimodal_awareness.emotional: emotional turning points, atmosphere shifts → flag [MEDIA: image].

media_opportunity_scan._principle: Do not force a fixed media checklist. Before assigning [MEDIA: ...] hints, scan what the material naturally supports. Aim for richness and variety when the data supports it, but never add video, audio, maps, or generated assets merely to satisfy a quota. If a normally tempting medium would be forced or decorative, set media_placeholder to null and explain in editorial_notes.
media_opportunity_scan.time_or_sequence: trend chart, timeline, scrollytelling, animation, or sonification if rhythm helps.
media_opportunity_scan.geography_or_routes: map, flow view, route animation, or location cards.
media_opportunity_scan.hierarchy_ranking_distribution: chart, treemap, sortable table, quiz, or stat callout.
media_opportunity_scan.network_relationships: node-link view, Sankey, adjacency matrix, or interactive explorer.
media_opportunity_scan.individual_cases: card deck, image, instance embed, quote browser, or annotated profile.
media_opportunity_scan.visual_subject_matter: images or video when the subject is inherently seen: animals, places, art, food, fashion, objects, sports, architecture.
media_opportunity_scan.sound_speech_music: audio only when hearing adds meaning, evidence, atmosphere, or embodied understanding.
media_opportunity_scan.abstract_interpretation: text-only can be the right choice.

audio_restraint: Audio's mandatory form is a REAL sourced background track the reader can play while reading (mood/immersion), chosen to fit the story and presented as a now-playing card — never AI-composed — so the front BGM is required on EVERY blog: always carry [MEDIA: audio] for it. BGM is never skipped, including on sober/computational/privacy topics (a restrained pensive/ambient track there is the RIGHT BGM, not filler) — the Scout walks the BGM ladder from a real sourced track at the top down to the license-clean classical-recording floor as the guaranteed bottom rung, so a fitting track always exists. An optional atmospheric sound_design SFX cue (text2music) is fine only for a needed sound with no findable real recording, and is never the front BGM. Reach for a sonification only when the data has a genuinely decodable sonic pattern. The BGM autostarts on the reader's first click/tap, then is reader-controlled; the page must work fully when muted.
